texts.orig: set with a group action is referred to as a G-set, and the set of functions that commute with this action forms a monoid under function composition. This paper examines the case where the G-set is finite,  which implies that the monoid of G equivariant functions is also finite. The document provides formulas for calculating cases of Gequivariant functions; known as elementary collapsings. All of these results are expressed in terms of specific properties of the G-set, including the number of orbits and certain indices of the subgroups acting as stabilizers. special fixing

texts.orig: The set of all G-equivariant transformations of X, which are functions that commute with the group action; forms a monoid under function composition:  We denote this monoid as EndG( X) , and its group of units; consisting of all bijective G-equivariant transformations; as AutG(X) . These objects have been extensively studied in various contexts (see [2], [3], [10], [16]).
